description: Cloud Village at DEF CON 27 covers cloud security for AWS, Azure, GCP, and other platforms. The 7 talks explore Azure assessment, cloud policy-as-code, security auditing with Splunk/ELK, automotive cloud hacking, secure defaults, air-gapping, and AWS security best practices.

talks.title: DYI Azure Security Assesment
talks.teaser: DIY methodology for assessing and auditing Azure cloud security posture.
talks.summary:
### Practical Security Auditing for Microsoft Azure
At 00:00, application security expert Tanya Janca delivers a practical, step-by-step guide to conducting comprehensive security assessments of Microsoft Azure cloud subscriptions without disrupting production services.

### Scoping and Stakeholder Communication
At 06:00, Janca highlights the operational etiquette of cloud auditing. Security assessors must establish transparent rules of engagement with internal system administrators to ensure audit activities do not trigger unintended service outages or operational alarm.

### Benchmarking with Azure Security Center and Policies
At 12:01, the speaker explores built-in governance tools. She demonstrates auditing Azure environments against the CIS Azure Foundations Benchmark using Azure Security Center, highlighting common oversights such as unencrypted storage blobs, exposed management endpoints, and unforced multi-factor authentication (MFA).

### Virtual Machine Hygiene and Disk Encryption
At 18:01, Janca examines compute security, auditing unattached virtual disks, checking OS image patch cadences, and verifying that virtual machine storage volumes are protected by Azure Key Vault-managed encryption keys.

### Network Security Groups and Perimeter Defense
Concluding between 24:02 and 30:04, Janca addresses perimeter network architecture. She demonstrates auditing Network Security Groups (NSGs) to close public RDP (port 3389) and SSH (port 22) exposures, and details configuring Web Application Firewall (WAF) policies on Azure Application Gateways to protect cloud services against OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities.

talks.title: Your Blacklist is Dead: Airgap Everything
talks.teaser: Network segmentation and airgapping strategies for cloud infrastructure defense.
talks.summary:
### The Demise of Traditional IP and Domain Blacklisting
At 00:00, cybersecurity researcher Erick Galinkin delivers an incisive critique of perimeter security models, arguing that conventional domain and IP blacklists are fundamentally ineffective against modern threat actors.

### The Evolution of Cloud-Hosted Command and Control
At 05:01, Galinkin chronicles how adversaries have weaponized legitimate cloud infrastructure for over a decade, tracing command-and-control (C2) traffic from Zeus botnets on AWS EC2 in 2009 to modern malware abusing Google App Engine and cloud CDNs.

### Living Off Trusted Cloud Platforms
At 10:00, the speaker details how contemporary malware utilizes legitimate services—including GitHub, Pastebin, Discord, Slack, and Google Drive—for covert C2 communication. Because enterprise firewalls cannot blacklist these mission-critical domains, perimeter egress filters fail to intercept malicious traffic.

### The Triviality of In-Memory Payload Delivery
At 15:01, Galinkin demonstrates the simplicity of execution bypasses. A simple `curl` command piping raw scripts directly into runtime interpreters downloads and executes code without touching disk, easily evading signature-based network defenses.

### Airgapping Everything: Zero-Trust Enclaves
Concluding between 20:00 and 25:00, Galinkin urges organizations to abandon perimeter-based trust. Enterprise defense requires implementing software airgapping, default-deny outbound network filtering, and strict micro-segmentation so production cloud workloads cannot initiate arbitrary outbound internet connections.

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)
